sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 22 of Employees Compensation Act seeking compensation together with interest thereon at the rate of 18% p.a., from the date of accident till the date of realization.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 20.03.2019 the petitioner No.1 son by name Roshan Basha was traveling from Guruguntepalya to Jalahalli Cross to deliver Mahindra XUV 500 bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AC-9923.

At the time at about 11:30 p.m the said vehicle met with an accident near Peenya Metro Station and because of the said accident Roshan Basha who is accompanied by one Abdul Rahman, who is the brother of Roshan Basha was grievously injured.
It is further urged that the said Roshan Basha was treated exhaustively in Hosmat Hospital as well as People Tree and Baptist Hospital and spend lakhs of rupees.
Even after the best efforts made by the doctors, he could not survive and he breathed his last on 10.04.2019.

It is further submitted that the accident had happened when the Roshan Basha was under the employment of respondent No.1 and there is an employer and employee relationship between the deceased and respondent No.1.

It is it is specifically submitted that the deceased was a driver by profession and was also working as an office boy and earning Rs.25,000/- per month including all incentives and due to the sudden demise of the deceased the family of the deceased are suffered great grief and hence prayed to allow the petition and directed respondents to pay compensation to the tune of Rs.1,17,00,000/- along with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
Hence prayed to award compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.

4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Mahindra XUV 500 bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AC-9923.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.1 has not complied with the provisions of Employees Act.
Further this respondent No.2 urged that there is no jural relationship of employer and employee between the deceased and respondent No.1.

It is contended that there is no nexus between the death of deceased and injuries suffered in alleged accident and as per police records the accident was taken place on 26.03.2019 and the deceased was died on 10.04.2019.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car / deceased did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Further it is urged that as on the date of accident the insured car did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioners that, on 26.03.2019 the accident had happened near Peenya Metro Station.
The factum of accident is not in dispute.
The only seminal question to be considered is whether the said accident had happened during the course of employment or not.
The time of accident, place plays an important role in assessing the rival contentions urged by the both the parties.
The accident had happened at 11:30 p.m.
It is the specific contention of the respondent No.2 that, the accident had happened when the deceased was going in a car for his personal work and not as a driver of 1st respondent.
On the other hand, it is the specific contention of the petitioners that, the deceased was under the employment of the respondent No.1 at the time of accident.
This being the rival contentions urged by the combating parties it is relevant to dwell into the documentary as well as the oral evidence.
Ex.P.2 is the FIS filed on 27.03.2019 at about 4.00 p.m.
The accident happened on 26.03.2019 at about 12.00 a.m.
There is absolutely no delay in filing FIS.
FIS was filed by one Anil Kumar, the Manager of respondent No.1 company.
He during the course of FIS itself had categorically stated that the deceased was working as a delivery executive in RW.1 firm.
It is needless to explain the nomenclature of delivery executive which presupposes that the deceased was driver working in respondent No.1 company.
In FIS itself it is made clear that when the deceased about to deliver the vehicle to the customer he met with an accident.
FIR is also lodged as per Ex.P1 which has its genesis in Ex.P2.

The whole defence of the respondent No.2 is based on the admission of PW1 during the course of cross examination which reads as hereunder :
"It is true to suggest that the accident was occurred when the deceased and Abdul Rahman were proceeding in a car in order to have the dinner."

By relying on this part of cross-examination, it is strenuously argued by learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that the accident happened out of employment and it does not have any nexus with the employment of deceased with respondent No.1.
Apart from this stray admission, there is absolutely no materials is placed on record by the respondent No.2 that the deceased was out of employment.
It is pertinent to note that the said stray sentence has no sanctity in the eye of law.
It is not relevant U/Sec.17 of Indian Evidence Act.
Only basing on this stray sentence of PW.1 the case of the petitioners cannot be distrusted.
It is settled principles of law that evidentiary admissions has to be crystal clear .
The stray admission in isolation cannot be taken into consideration.

In this regard,
it is pertinent to rely on a decision reported in:-
2010(2) K.L.J. 457 (Bayamma and others Vs. Puttabayamma and another) wherein Hon'ble Karnataka High Court held as hereunder:-
"In so far as the second contention that there has been admission in the cross- examination is concerned, the positive case of the plaintiff in her pleadings as well as in the evidence is in support of the case for the reliefs prayed for.

sentences.text: A stray admission to the effect that there was no interference since the year 1967, cannot over-turn the entire pleadings and evidence to contend otherwise.
It is wholly unjust to rely on such a stray statement being recorded to over turn the case of the plaintiff to hold that there was no cause of action.
This is not a substantial question of law which would warrant interference by this court even if it could be said that there was an error in the reasoning of the Courts below."

The above said stray admission of PW.1 does not have any backing of documentary proof.
When such is the case the said admission is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners herein.
15. Another important aspect to be noted herein is the inquest which was drawn as per Ex.P.11.
This court gave its anxious consideration to the contents of the inquest report.

On close perusal of the contents of the inquest report it reflects that the relatives of the deceased had given a statement before the police that, when the deceased was about to deliver the vehicle he met with an accident.
There is a doctrine under law called Notional Extension Theory which is aptly applicable to the case on hand.

Before applying the notional extension theory to the facts of the instant case on hand, it is relevant to conceptual aspects of notional extension theory :
The doctrine of notional extension theory emerges from the concept of social security.
It extends the concept of employment beyond the boundaries.
This doctrine prescribes that the compensation to be paid be paid to the workers in case of accident during the coarse of employment.
According to Merriam Webster dictionary, notional meaning theoretical, speculative estimate and hypothetical and it's an imaginary thing causes due to lack of perfection or no evident.

Generally notional extension of employment means a hypothetical or imaginary extension of the employment period of employees in certain circumstances for provisional benefits under various laws by employer.

The doctrine of notional extension mentioned under Section 3 of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 said that it is the legal obligation of an employer to provide damages to their employees, their family members in situations where injury are inflicted during working hours at the workplace.

Section 3 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923, now called as Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 states about the employer's liability for compensation and the doctrine of notional extension has evolved from this section only.

Section 3(1) of the said Act sates that "if personal injury is caused to an employee by accident arising out of and in the course of his employment: his employer shall be liable to pay compensation in accordance with the Chapter II of Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923.

As a rule, the employment of a workman does not commence until he has reached the place of employment and does not continue when he has left the place of employment, the journey to and from the place of employment being excluded.

It is Zareenunnisa vs Prime Mover Mobility Tech Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189047108/
6 now well-settled, however, that this is subject to the theory of notional extension of the employer's premises so as to include an area which theworkman passes and repasses in going to and in leaving the actual place of work.

sentences.text: There may be some reasonable extension in both time and place and a workman may be regarded as in the course of his employment even though he had not reached or had left his employer's premises.
16. Reverting back to the factual matrix the petitioners have also produced the attendance register through PW.4 at Ex.P.34.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that the deceased had attended the duty on the ill-fated day of accident.
While on his way to deliver the vehicle, the deceased might have taken diversion to have the food.
That admission of PW1 itself is not a conclusive proof to conclude that the deceased was out of employment.
The petitioners have produced the pick-up and delivery hub screen of the respondent No.1.

On close perusal of the same it reflects that the vehicle was given to the deceased at 9.00 p.m. When such is the case, on his way to deliver the vehicle he might have gone to have a food and the said fact comes within the sphere and ambit of notional extension theory.

17. Further more the petitioners have also got examined the Investigating Officer as PW.2 he during his chief-examination had produced the RC and insurance of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.K03-AC-9823 and has also produced the driving license of the deceased.
Only for the reason that the deceased was accompanied by Sri.Abdul Rahman who is the brother of the deceased it does not means that he was out of employment.
This court can concede the fact that the accident happened at a late night at 11:30 p.m.
The deceased was going to deliver the car to the customer.
When such is the case he might have taken his brother along with him to deliver the car at the late night.
The fact that the deceased was accompanied by his brother Abdul Rahman itself does not means that the deceased was out of employment.
The claimants have made the best efforts and have succeeded in demonstrating that the accident had happened during the course of employment.
Even PW.4 being the Assistant Fleet Manager at PrimeMover Mobility Technologies Pvt. Ltd., have also supported the case of the claimants.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of petitioners.
On assessing entire evidence in the light of oral and documentary evidence, the preponderance of probabilities tilts in favour of the petitioners.

Hence this Court answers issue No.2 'In the Affirmative'.
18. Issue No.1 : This issues revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the question of proving the employer and employee relationship between Respondent No.1 and deceased.
The Respondent No.1 has appeared before the court but did not choose to file any written statement.
The claimants have got examined one Naveen. G who is the Fleet Assistant Manager at respondent No.1 company through him Ex.P.31 to 34 were marked.
Ex.P.31 is the Offer Letter which employment of deceased and Ex.P.33 is the Employee Joining Form with documents.
These two documents clears all mists created by the respondent No.2 around the case of the petitioners.
These two documents categorically reflects that the deceased was working in respondent No.1 company.
Further, more PW.4 has also produced pay slips at Ex.P.32, which further depicts as to the employer and employee relationship of the deceased.
Though he was cross-examined by respondent No.2 counsel at length but nothing fatal has been elicited during the course of cross examination.

The death benefits given Zareenunnisa vs Prime Mover Mobility Tech Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189047108/
7 to the family of the deceased after the death of deceased also reflects that the accident had happened during the employment.

sentences.text: Much vociferous arguments have been addressed by the respondent.No.2 counsel by relying on Ex.P.31 and 33 documents stating that the deceased was not a driver in the company.
The designation of the deceased is Delivery Executive.
As discussed supra, the Delivery Executive presupposes that he is a driver.
When such is the case the evidence of PW4 Coupled with Ex.P31 to 34 documents set at knot all the contentions urged by the respondent No.2.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the relationship of master and servant between the respondent No.1 and the deceased, but the said contention is neutralized by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 has to be accepted.
Thereby holding that the deceased sustained injuries during the course of his employment.

This Court answers issues No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
19. ISSUE NO.3:
The petitioners claim that, Petitioner.No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the sister of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhaar card and ration marked at Ex's.P.13 to 15 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers issue No.3 In the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.4 :
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.1,17,00,000/- on the death of deceased Roshan Basha in the road traffic accident.
It is it is specifically submitted that the deceased was a driver by profession and was also working as an office boy and earning Rs.25,000/- per month including all incentives.
In order to prove the same the claimants have got examined one Naveen. G who is the Fleet Assistant Manager at respondent No.1 company through him Ex.P.31 to 34 were marked.

Ex.P.31 is the Offer Letter which employment of deceased, Ex.P.22 is the Pay slips, Ex.P.33 is the Employee Joining Form with documents and ExP.34 is the Attendance register form from December 2018 to March-2019.
These documents clears all mists created by the respondent No.2 around the case of the petitioners and they categorically reflects that the deceased was working in respondent No.1 company.

PW.2 wherein during the course of cross examination he categorically admitted that the deceased was working in their company as a driver and they have maintain online wage register and they have give PF, ESI and such other benefits to their employees.

On close perusal of Ex.P.32 salary slips it reflects that, the total earnings is Rs.16,368/- on further it is mentioned the Over time amount and the said amount is varied from month to month and that is paid only extra hours working.
Hence the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,368/-.
Therefore, Rs.16,368/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
21. This issues revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the quantum of compensation.
The petitioners have got exhibited the Aadhar card of the deceased which is marked as Ex.P14 wherein his year of birth is reflected as 1995.
This indicates that he was aged 24 years on the date of accident.

sentences.text: Accordingly the income of deceased is taken as Rs.16,368/- per month.

As per Section 4 of Employee's Compensation Act, the compensation payable to the legal representatives of the deceased employee shall be an amount equal to 50% of the monthly wages of the said employee multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, whichever is more.
50% of Rs.16,368/- works out to Rs.8,184/-.
Relevant factor is 219.95.
Hence, compensation payable to the petitioners would be Rs.8,184 x 219.95 = Rs.18,00,070/- which is rounded off to Rs.18,00,000/-.
Further the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses of the deceased.
23. PW.1 has produced 48-medical bills which are marked at Ex.P16.
As per that, the claimants have spent Rs.5,73,952.07/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
All these bills have been meticulously examined and are found to be correct.
Hence an amount of Rs.5,73,952.07/- which is rounded off to Rs.5,74,000/- is awarded to the petitioners towards the medical expenses of the deceased.

24. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Compensation for the death : 18,00,000-00 of the deceased 2 Funeral expenses of the : 18,150-00 deceased 3 Medical expenses of the : 5,74,000-00 deceased Total 23,92,150-00 25.
INTEREST & LIABILITY :

Relying upon the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in AIR 2014 SUPREME COURT 1393 (Saberabibi Yakubbhai Saikh vs. National insurance Co Ltd., and others), this court hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of incident i.e., 26.03.2019 till the date of realization.

27. ISSUE NO.5:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed u/s.22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,92,150/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of incident till its realization.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Apart from this stray admission, there is absolutely no materials is placed on record by the respondent No.2 that the deceased was out of employment.
It is pertinent to note that the said stray sentence has no sanctity in the eye of law.
It is not relevant U/Sec.17 of Indian Evidence Act.
Only basing on this stray sentence of PW.1 the case of the petitioners cannot be distrusted.
It is settled principles of law that evidentiary admissions has to be crystal clear .
The stray admission in isolation cannot be taken into consideration.
Zareenunnisa vs Prime Mover Mobility Tech Pvt Ltd on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189047108/
5 2007(3) KLJ 28 (Puttanna Shetty (deceased) by LRS Vs. Smt. Padma Shetty (deceased) by LRS and others wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "Admission - Civil proceedings - Has to be clear - To be read in the light of pleadings and other evidence - One stray sentence cannot be picked up".
AIR 1981 Karnataka 80 (Smt. Parameshwari Bai Vs. Muthojirao Scindia, Bangalore) wherein Hon'ble Karnataka High Court held that, "Evidence Act - Section 17 - Admission during examination - Evidence should be read as a whole".
The above said stray admission of PW.1 does not have any backing of documentary proof.
When such is the case the said admission is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners herein.
There may be some reasonable extension in both time and place and a workman may be regarded as in the course of his employment even though he had not reached or had left his employer's premises.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that the deceased had attended the duty on the ill-fated day of accident.
While on his way to deliver the vehicle, the deceased might have taken diversion to have the food.
That admission of PW1 itself is not a conclusive proof to conclude that the deceased was out of employment.
The petitioners have produced the pick-up and delivery hub screen of the respondent No.1.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that the vehicle was given to the deceased at 9.00 p.m. When such is the case, on his way to deliver the vehicle he might have gone to have a food and the said fact comes within the sphere and ambit of notional extension theory.
Only for the reason that the deceased was accompanied by Sri.Abdul Rahman who is the brother of the deceased it does not means that he was out of employment.
The deceased was going to deliver the car to the customer.
When such is the case he might have taken his brother along with him to deliver the car at the late night.
On assessing entire evidence in the light of oral and documentary evidence, the preponderance of probabilities tilts in favour of the petitioners.
The designation of the deceased is Delivery Executive.
When such is the case the evidence of PW4 Coupled with Ex.P31 to 34 documents set at knot all the contentions urged by the respondent No.2.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 has to be accepted.
Thereby holding that the deceased sustained injuries during the course of his employment.
Relying upon the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in AIR 2014 SUPREME COURT 1393 (Saberabibi Yakubbhai Saikh vs. National insurance Co Ltd., and others), this court hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of incident i.e., 26.03.2019 till the date of realization.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly the income of deceased is taken as Rs.16,368/- per month.
As per Section 4 of Employee's Compensation Act, the compensation payable to the legal representatives of the deceased employee shall be an amount equal to 50% of the monthly wages of the said employee multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, whichever is more.
50% of Rs.16,368/- works out to Rs.8,184/-.
Relevant factor is 219.95.
Hence, compensation payable to the petitioners would be Rs.8,184 x 219.95 = Rs.18,00,070/- which is rounded off to Rs.18,00,000/-.
Further the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses of the deceased.
As per that, the claimants have spent Rs.5,73,952.07/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
Hence an amount of Rs.5,73,952.07/- which is rounded off to Rs.5,74,000/- is awarded to the petitioners towards the medical expenses of the deceased.
INTEREST & LIABILITY :
26. The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 12% p.a., from the date of the incident till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
27. ISSUE NO.5:
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed u/s.22 of Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,92,150/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of incident till its realization.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit, the share of entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioners No.2 through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
